key_points: US President Donald Trump's extension of the $100,000 H-1B visa fee led to a 92% decrease in registrations, adding pressure to IT stocks.
items.summary: OFSS shares plunged to Rs 11,061, becoming the top loser on the Nifty IT index. This decline follows reports that Oracle's $18 billion data centre debt is under pressure due to opposition to its New Mexico campus. Additionally, US President Donald Trump extended the $100,000 H-1B visa fee, which led to a 92% decrease in registrations by large IT outsourcing firms, contributing to broader sector pressure.
items.title: IT stocks fall as Oracle debt and H-1B fee concerns weigh on sector

key_points: The paper compares official government data with alternative sources for tracking U.S. semiconductor manufacturing investment, noting limitations in the former and validating the latter through a 2023 comparison.
items.summary: This NBER working paper by Byrne, Kurtzman, and Williams evaluates methods for measuring U.S. semiconductor manufacturing investment. The authors note that official government sources face limitations due to broad categories and publication lags. In contrast, alternative data from SEMI offers greater timeliness and specificity. Comparing SEMI data with official statistics through 2023 showed broad consistency, validating SEMI as a credible supplement.
items.title: Study Evaluates U.S. Semiconductor Investment Tracking Methods

key_points: Instagram restricted the Stop Vizag Data Centers account in India, alleging legal compliance while the movement claims lack of prior communication.
The campaign, which opposed AI data centers in Visakhapatnam, announced a backup account and plans to continue public awareness efforts.
items.summary: Instagram restricted the 'Stop Vizag Data Centers' account in India, making it unavailable to local users while remaining accessible internationally. Representatives of the movement allege the restriction was imposed without prior communication. The campaign, which opposes AI data centers in Visakhapatnam, has announced a backup account to continue its advocacy. The account had garnered over 56 lakh views and 11,800 followers in two months before the block.
items.title: Instagram restricts Stop Vizag Data Centers account in India

key_points: Tata Group stocks faced pressure on Monday as the dispute between Tata Trusts and Tata Sons over leadership escalated, with investors watching for legal proceedings.
Tata Trusts alleges Tata Sons improperly reappointed N Chandrasekaran using a casting vote despite a director opposing the resolution, challenging the decision's validity.
items.summary: Tata Group stocks remained under pressure during Monday's trading session as the dispute between Tata Trusts and Tata Sons over leadership and the conglomerate's future structure intensified. Investors are closely monitoring the situation for potential legal proceedings and renewed uncertainty surrounding Tata Sons' proposed listing. The immediate trigger is a disagreement over the reappointment of Chairman N Chandrasekaran. Tata Trusts alleges that the Tata Sons board went ahead with a five-year term for Chandrasekaran based on a casting vote, despite one of its two nominees voting against the resolution.
items.title: Tata Group stocks fall as Trusts-Sons leadership dispute deepens

key_points: The Reserve Bank of India has amended KYC rules to allow Indian banks to accept documents certified by officials outside India.
FPI outflows remain elevated due to global conflicts and high bond yields, though India's growth offers support.
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has simplified Know Your Customer compliance for foreign portfolio investors, effective immediately. Under the 2026 amendment, Indian banks can now accept documents certified by authorised officials abroad, including notaries and embassy officials, rather than requiring certification within India. This change aims to ease documentation for overseas investors. Meanwhile, FPI outflows reached ₹23,676 crore in September amid global tensions and high US bond yields, though India's economic resilience may support future inflows.
items.title: RBI Simplifies KYC Rules for Foreign Portfolio Investors

key_points: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated there is a 0% chance AI will cause human extinction by 2030.
Huang dismissed recent warnings from researchers as irresponsible doomsday narratives not grounded in science.
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang rejected assertions that artificial intelligence poses an extinction risk to humanity within the next decade. Speaking to CBS News, Huang declared a 0% probability of such an event by 2030, labeling recent warnings as irresponsible doomsday narratives. While other industry leaders like Elon Musk and Dario Amodei have called for development slowdowns, Huang emphasized that his company's success relies on safe deployment and existing cybersecurity laws.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Rejects AI Extinction Claims by 2030

key_points: Under President Lula, Amazon deforestation reached a 10-year low, but experts warn a potential victory by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro could reverse these gains and reinstate policies favoring agribusiness and mining.

The upcoming election is viewed as a critical juncture for Brazil's environmental stance, with a shift in leadership potentially disrupting international climate targets and jeopardizing access to European markets due to deforestation regulations.

Recent conservation successes in Indigenous territories and protected areas have been achieved through federal enforcement, yet these gains remain fragile amid legislative rollbacks and security challenges that threaten to undo progress.
items.summary: Under President Lula, Amazon deforestation dropped to a 10-year low, yet experts warn that a potential victory by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro could reinstate policies favoring agribusiness and mining, reversing recent progress. The upcoming election is seen as a high-stakes contest determining Brazil's adherence to global environmental targets and its role in international climate diplomacy. While federal enforcement has successfully reduced deforestation in specific Indigenous territories, these gains are described as fragile. Analysts caution that a policy shift could disrupt international funding and jeopardize Brazil's commitments to cut emissions and eliminate illegal deforestation by 2030.
items.title: Brazil Election Looms Over Amazon Conservation Future

key_points: Three Indian cybersecurity researchers from Hacktron AI used Anthropic's Claude to identify security vulnerabilities in OpenAI's systems, gaining access to employee accounts and private repositories within 72 hours under a bug bounty program.
items.summary: Three Indian cybersecurity researchers from Hacktron AI used Anthropic's AI chatbot Claude to identify security vulnerabilities in OpenAI's systems. Under OpenAI's bug bounty program, they exploited these flaws to access employee accounts and private GitHub repositories within 72 hours. OpenAI subsequently patched the issues and awarded the team approximately 6,500 dollars as a bounty.
items.title: Three Indian Researchers Used Claude to Find OpenAI Security Flaws

key_points: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dismissed warnings that AI could cause humanity's extinction by 2030 as unfounded doomsday narratives.
Huang stated there is a 0% chance of such an outcome and argued that slowing AI development might be a strategy to avoid liability.
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang rejected recent warnings that artificial intelligence could lead to humanity's extinction by 2030, calling them 'doomsday narratives' with a 0% chance of occurring. Speaking to CBS News, Huang argued that slowing AI development is not grounded in science and may be an attempt by firms to seek liability protections. While researchers and executives like Dario Amodei and Sam Altman have urged caution, Huang emphasized that Nvidia's success depends on the safe deployment of its products. The comments follow a broader debate on AI safety, with US and Chinese officials recently discussing new safety mechanisms.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Rejects AI Extinction Fears

key_points: Apple increased iPhone prices by £100 across all models, including older ones, due to a severe shortage of memory chips driven by AI demand.
Industry experts warn that higher component costs will persist, with memory prices expected to rise until 2027 and smartphone prices unlikely to return to previous levels.
The price hike affects not only Apple but also other electronics manufacturers, including Microsoft and Dell, as memory costs have surged globally.
items.summary: Apple raised the price of all its iPhones by £100, including older models, following a severe shortage of memory chips driven by the AI industry's demand. Francisco Jeronimo of IDC attributes this to 'RAMageddon,' where memory costs have risen over 300% year-on-year. While Apple is the most affected due to its global sales volume, other manufacturers like Microsoft and Dell have also increased prices. Experts warn that these higher costs are likely to persist, with memory prices expected to remain elevated until 2027, marking the end of the era of cheap smartphones.
items.title: Apple raises iPhone prices by £100 due to memory chip shortage

key_points: Content creator Pragati successfully recovered her lost iPhone 16 Pro for the fifth time in Japan after realizing it was missing several hours later.
She attributed the safe recovery to Japan's low crime rate and used Apple's 'Find My' feature to locate the device approximately 600 metres away.
Viewers commented on the safety of Japan compared to other countries, noting that theft is rare due to social norms rather than just law enforcement.
items.summary: Content creator Pragati recently shared a video documenting her fifth successful recovery of a lost iPhone 16 Pro in Japan. After realizing the device was missing several hours later, she used Apple's 'Find My' feature to locate it approximately 600 metres away. Pragati attributed the safe recovery to Japan's renowned civic safety and low crime rate. The video sparked a conversation about public safety, with viewers comparing Japan's environment to other countries like Dubai and India. Pragati noted that the phone was found completely undisturbed despite being left unattended in public for hours.
items.title: Indian Woman Recovers Lost iPhone 16 Pro Five Times in Japan

key_points: An Apple store in Canberra was sued for indirect discrimination after using a disabled bathroom for storage and as a change room.
items.summary: An Apple store in Canberra Centre faced legal action for indirect discrimination after utilizing a disabled bathroom for storage and as a change room, forcing an employee with a disability to wait for standard toilets. While the ACT Civil and Administrative Tribunal dismissed complaints regarding direct discrimination, it awarded the former employee $18,000 in damages for the indirect discrimination experienced.
items.title: Apple Store Sued Over Disabled Bathroom Misuse

key_points: The proceeds will finance a follow-on investment in OpenAI expected to close next month, while the deal may price on Thursday.
items.summary: SoftBank Group is seeking more than $11 billion in junk bonds to fund its investments in OpenAI, according to people familiar with the matter. The company plans to issue $10 billion in dollar securities and €1 billion in euro notes. The funds will partly finance a follow-on investment in OpenAI expected to close next month. SoftBank, which has committed close to $65 billion to the tech pioneer, may price the deal on Thursday as safety concerns in the AI industry have flared.
items.title: SoftBank Raises $11 Billion for OpenAI Bet

key_points: Indigenous Chief Wagner Karipuna warns that offshore oil exploration near his village in the Brazilian Amazon puts communities at risk of spills and environmental damage.
Petrobras states that while production is not expected for six or seven years, it has identified oil signs 175 kilometers off the coast and maintains continuous dialogue with local communities.
Local residents hold mixed views, with some fearing displacement and economic ruin while others see potential wealth and job creation from the project.
items.summary: Indigenous Chief Wagner Karipuna in Oiapoque, Brazil, expresses deep concern over offshore oil exploration by Petrobras near his village, fearing potential spills could devastate the local environment and economy. While Petrobras reports identifying oil signs 175 kilometers off the coast and states production is not expected for six or seven years, it maintains that spill risks are low. The project has sparked divided reactions; some residents anticipate economic benefits and job creation, while others, including fishermen and the chief, worry about displacement, infrastructure strain, and the long-term consequences of potential oil leaks in the region.
items.title: Indigenous Leader Warns of Oil Risks in Brazilian Amazon

key_points: The Singapore Business Federation launched a new diagnostic tool to help companies assess their future readiness and identify capability gaps.
Pilot data shows that while many companies aspire to improve, they currently lack the capabilities to reach their targets, particularly in technology and skills.
The tool measures maturity rather than just activity, providing actionable insights to guide businesses toward becoming future-ready by 2027.
items.summary: The Singapore Business Federation (SBF) launched the Future Ready Business Index (FRBI), a holistic diagnostic tool developed with Boston Consulting Group and partners, to help firms assess their future readiness. The tool evaluates 11 quantitative measures and 39 qualitative metrics across six dimensions, including success-driven performance and smart-enabled technology. Based on a pilot with 102 companies, Mariam Jaafar of BCG noted that while 77% of respondents aspire to be future-ready by 2027, about 80% are currently in nascent or emerging stages. The FRBI distinguishes itself by measuring maturity rather than just activity and turning diagnosis into actionable steps, with SBF recommending retakes every two years to track progress.
items.title: SBF Launches Tool to Assess Future Business Readiness

key_points: Starbucks signed an agreement with the Tamil Nadu government to establish a global capability centre in Chennai.
The new facility is expected to create approximately 800 technology jobs.
items.summary: Starbucks has signed a pact with the Tamil Nadu state government to set up a global capability centre in Chennai. The Tamil Nadu government stated on Sept 21 that the project will create roughly 800 technology jobs. Starbucks, which operates about 500 cafes in India via a joint venture with Tata Consumer Products, did not immediately comment on the agreement.
items.title: Starbucks Plans Global Tech Centre in Chennai, India

key_points: Outage tracker Downdetector recorded thousands of reports for the platforms before they largely recovered by early Tuesday.
items.summary: Users in Singapore and other countries reported access issues with Facebook and Instagram on Monday morning. Outage tracker Downdetector showed reports peaking around 9.20am in Singapore, with thousands of reports recorded in the US. Reports of outages fell sharply by 2am GMT, indicating the services had largely recovered. The platforms, owned by Meta, have experienced other outages this year.
items.title: Facebook and Instagram Face Brief Global Outage

key_points: Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng leads a delegation to the US for economic and trade consultations from September 19 to 23, following a series of balanced outcomes since the May summit.

The US services trade surplus with China reached $34.4 billion in 2025, while US affiliates in China generated over $640 billion in revenue in 2023, highlighting the complementary strengths of both economies.
Business groups from both nations are calling for expanded cooperation, with AmCham Shanghai reporting that member company profitability in China rebounded to its highest level since 2019 in 2025.
items.summary: Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng is leading a delegation to the United States for economic and trade consultations scheduled from September 19 to 23. These talks aim to address mutual concerns and build on the consensus reached during a historic summit in Beijing in May. Recent data indicates that the US services trade surplus with China stood at $34.4 billion in 2025, while US affiliates in China generated more than $640 billion in revenue in 2023. Business organizations from both countries are urging for expanded cooperation, with the American Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai noting a significant rebound in member company profitability in China.
items.title: China-US Trade Talks Resume Amidst Ongoing Tariff Discussions

key_points: ScrollEd, a Palo Alto startup, is pitching an app that converts textbooks into short-form video feeds similar to TikTok.
items.summary: ScrollEd, a Palo Alto startup, is pitching an app that converts textbooks into short-form video feeds similar to TikTok. Co-founder Utsav Gupta states the platform aims to meet younger users where they are by making deep learning as easy as swiping through videos. The company plans to launch its consumer business at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco, targeting students and educational institutions with a freemium model.
items.title: ScrollEd Aims to Transform Textbooks into TikTok-Style Feeds

key_points: The system features a stacked-cell architecture and AI-based thermal management, aiming to reduce auxiliary power consumption by 30% while addressing supply constraints associated with lithium-ion batteries.
items.summary: Energy storage manufacturer HiTHIUM has unveiled a 4 MWh sodium-ion battery storage system designed for a 30-year service life. The company stated that full-scale production and deliveries are planned to begin in 2027. HiTHIUM CTO Dr Nazar Yi noted the technology aims to address cost and resource availability as energy storage deployment expands. The system utilizes a stacked-cell architecture and AI-based thermal management to optimize efficiency and reduce footprint. While the technology remains less established commercially than lithium-ion, HiTHIUM intends to initially target utility-scale storage applications.
items.title: HiTHIUM Unveils 4 MWh Sodium-Ion Battery System Targeting 2027 Production

key_points: The paper analyzes how the U.S.-China trade war has altered global trade flows, causing Chinese exports to shift away from the U.S. toward third countries.
items.summary: Pol Antràs, Adrian Kulesza, and Andrea F. Presbitero study how the U.S.-China trade war reshaped global trade patterns, creating significant spillovers to third countries. Using recent tariff policy changes and monthly international trade flow data, the authors document a redirection of Chinese exports away from the U.S. market and toward third countries.
items.title: New Study Examines Global Trade Shifts Following U.S.-China Trade War

key_points: Microsoft India President Puneet Chandok announced a new cloud region in Hyderabad designed to use effectively zero water for cooling and support AI workloads from day one.
The facility represents a major investment with 630 megawatts of renewable energy already contracted, contributing to Microsoft's goal of being carbon negative by 2030.
items.summary: Puneet Chandok, President of Microsoft India and South Asia, announced the launch of the company's fourth cloud region in India, located in Hyderabad. Designed to handle AI workloads from the outset, the facility utilizes effectively zero water for cooling. The project includes 630 megawatts of contracted renewable energy and supports Microsoft's commitment to becoming carbon negative by 2030. Chandok noted that India currently has around 2 gigawatts of data center capacity, which could expand six to seven times by 2035.
items.title: Microsoft Announces Water-Efficient India Cloud Region for AI

key_points: Apple has initiated a second round of layoffs in less than two months, affecting the Fitness+ division.
According to Bloomberg, the cuts target the audio-content team, though features like Time to Walk will continue.
items.summary: Apple has announced a second round of layoffs in less than two months, impacting the Fitness+ division. A Bloomberg report indicates that the audio-content team, responsible for features such as Time to Walk and Time to Run, was affected. While the report suggests these features will not be discontinued, Apple plans to release new audio content less frequently due to the reduced team size.
items.title: Apple Announces Second Round of Layoffs in Fitness+ Division Within Two Months

key_points: The board approved Chandrasekaran's continuation in a 4-1 vote, but Tata Trusts challenged the decision, citing non-compliance with Articles of Association regarding Trust-nominated director approval.
items.summary: Tata Group stocks fell on Monday as investors tracked uncertainty surrounding Tata Sons' listing plans and the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as chairman. Shares of Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles fell more than 1%, while Tata Power declined around 2.3%. The Tata Sons board approved Chandrasekaran's continuation through a 4-1 vote, with Noel Tata opposing. However, Tata Trusts challenged the decision, arguing the resolution did not meet requirements under the Articles of Association because the required majority of Trust-nominated directors did not approve it. This disagreement adds uncertainty to Tata Sons' future leadership and potential market listing plans.
items.title: Tata Group Stocks Fall Amid Listing and Leadership Dispute

key_points: Meta's Facebook and Instagram services recovered in the U.S. following a brief outage that disrupted thousands of users on Sunday.
Downdetector tracked over 17,000 outage reports on Facebook and more than 5,000 on Instagram, though actual affected users may vary based on user submissions.
items.summary: Meta's social media platforms Facebook and Instagram recovered from a brief outage that disrupted service for thousands of users in the U.S. on Sunday, according to Downdetector.com. The disruption began around 8:55 p.m. ET and peaked with over 17,000 reports on Facebook and more than 5,000 on Instagram. Reports of outages fell sharply by about 10 p.m. ET, indicating services had largely recovered. Meta did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Since Downdetector numbers are based on user-submitted reports, the actual number of affected users may vary.
items.title: Meta Platforms Recover After Brief US Outage

key_points: Twenty crested ibises were released into the wild in Gansu Province, marking the highest-altitude rewilding effort in China.
The release follows three years of conservation work, with the population having produced 30 chicks since 2023.
items.summary: On September 20, 2026, twenty crested ibises were released into the wild at the Xiaolongshan forest area in Gansu Province, China. This event marks the westernmost and highest-altitude crested ibis rewilding effort in the country. The release signifies a shift from captive breeding to rebuilding a wild population, following three years of conservation work that saw the population produce 30 chicks since 2023.
items.title: Crested ibises released in China's westernmost rewilding effort

key_points: A RAND Corporation analysis of 1,181 AI firms shows a 61% to 26% split in pure software focus between American and Chinese companies.
While both nations utilize similar underlying technologies, American firms concentrate on healthcare and cybersecurity, whereas Chinese firms prioritize manufacturing and robotics.
Recent data indicates a shift in API traffic, with Chinese models gaining ground through lower costs, though American systems still lead in raw intelligence scores.
items.summary: A recent report by the RAND Corporation's Center on AI, Security, and Technology highlights a significant divergence in the strategic focus of US and Chinese artificial intelligence industries. While both nations utilize similar underlying technologies like transformer architecture, American firms predominantly develop pure software solutions for healthcare and cybersecurity, whereas Chinese companies concentrate on embodied intelligence for manufacturing and robotics. This distinction stems from differing economic structures and industrial policies. Although American models currently lead in raw intelligence, Chinese models are gaining market share by offering comparable performance at a fraction of the cost, reshaping the competitive landscape through price rather than pure capability.
items.title: RAND Report Reveals Divergent Paths in US and Chinese AI Development

key_points: Three Indian-origin men from Hacktron AI discovered an account-takeover vulnerability in OpenAI systems and received a $6,500 bounty.
Pedhapati Mohan Sri Rama Krishna, a Telugu-origin founder of Electrovolt Security, was one of the researchers who reported the flaw.
items.summary: Three Indian-origin researchers from Hacktron AI, including Pedhapati Mohan Sri Rama Krishna of Telugu origin, discovered an account-takeover vulnerability in OpenAI systems. They reported the flaw, which allowed unauthorized access to ChatGPT and Codex accounts via the OpenAI help forum. OpenAI coordinated a patch and paid the team a $6,500 bounty. Hacktron AI, founded in 2025, aims to secure internet-critical systems by identifying vulnerabilities before malicious actors.
items.title: Telugu-Origin Man Among Three Who Found OpenAI Vulnerabilities

key_points: The discussions occur amidst US sanctions on Russia and a new AI initiative, while China negotiates a reciprocal tariff reduction framework worth $30 billion from each side.
items.summary: US and Chinese officials held candid trade talks in New York focusing on AI and economic issues ahead of President Xi Jinping's upcoming visit to Washington. The discussions occurred amidst US sanctions on Russia and a new AI initiative, while China negotiated a reciprocal tariff reduction framework worth $30 billion from each side. Officials emphasized mutual respect and win-win cooperation during the exchanges.
items.title: US and China hold trade talks ahead of Xi's Washington visit

key_points: Chandigarh authorities have cancelled a proposed iPhone distribution event organized by influencer Rakesh Trehan, citing security concerns and the risk of overcrowding.
items.summary: Chandigarh authorities have cancelled a proposed iPhone distribution event organized by influencer Rakesh Trehan, citing security concerns and the risk of overcrowding. Trehan had planned to give away free iPhones to 10 lucky people out of 100 on September 22, but the event was stopped by police orders. The Deputy Commissioner directed the cancellation, suggesting Trehan use his resources for other forms of social service instead.
items.title: Chandigarh Authorities Cancel iPhone Langar Event Due to Security Risks

key_points: MSME Minister Kondapalli Srinivas stated that Mahakavi Gurajada Apparao's works will continue to inspire generations due to their portrayal of societal issues and human emotions.
On the writer's 164th birth anniversary, officials paid tributes at his historic house and held a rally to highlight his literary contributions.
items.summary: MSME Minister Kondapalli Srinivas stated that Mahakavi Gurajada Apparao's works, including 'Kanyasulkam', will continue to inspire generations because they portray societal issues and human emotions. On the writer's 164th birth anniversary, Srinivas, MLA Aditi Vijayalakshmi Gajapathi Raju, and Joint Collector Sedhu Madhavan paid tributes at his historic house and organized a rally to Gurajada Junction. The government declared the anniversary a State festival with celebrations across the region.
items.title: MSME Minister Kondapalli Srinivas Honors Mahakavi Gurajada Apparao on Birth Anniversary

key_points: Kharge highlighted that in West Bengal, 93 percent of decided appeals resulted in voter restoration, though over 37 lakh appeals remain pending in Delhi.
items.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge criticized the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, describing it as a flawed process that threatens democracy. He argued that the creation of a 'VIP' voter category violates the constitutional principle of equal voting rights. Citing West Bengal data where 93 percent of decided appeals resulted in voter restoration, Kharge noted that over 37 lakh appeals remain pending in Delhi, where notices have been issued to prominent figures including government officials and political leaders.
items.title: Congress President Kharge Criticizes Election Commission's SIR Process

key_points: The institute apologized for earlier statements regarding the incident and stated that details remain under investigation by appropriate authorities.
items.summary: IIT Bombay suspended Dean of Student Affairs Professor Suryanarayana Doolla following the suicide of student Sahil Wakode. The suspension occurred amidst student protests and demands for action. The institute issued an apology for earlier remarks concerning the incident, stating that details remain under investigation. Doolla will continue serving as a professor in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering.
items.title: IIT Bombay Suspends Dean Following Student Suicide and Apologizes for Remarks

key_points: HEG shares rose 5% after Replus Engitech Private was awarded a Rs 217.56 crore order for lithium-ion battery banks to be executed by March 31, 2027.
The company also announced a demerger plan separating its graphite electrodes business into HEG Graphite and retaining advanced materials and battery solutions in the existing entity.
items.summary: HEG shares rallied 5% following news that its subsidiary, Replus Engitech Private, secured a Rs 217.56 crore order for lithium-ion battery banks from a domestic entity, with execution due by March 31, 2027. Concurrently, the company outlined a demerger plan to split into HEG Graphite for graphite electrodes and HEG Advanced Materials for battery and green power businesses, while also amalgamating Bhilwara Energy into the existing structure.
items.title: HEG Shares Rally on Battery Order and Demerger News

key_points: China-US agricultural trade totaled $14.1 billion during the first half of 2026.
This volume equates to approximately $78 million worth of produce crossing the Pacific daily.
items.summary: According to BizDataDive, trade in fresh produce between China and the United States reached $14.1 billion in the first half of 2026. This transaction volume represents approximately $78 million worth of agricultural goods crossing the Pacific Ocean every day. The exchange includes American soybeans used in Chinese soy milk and Chinese garlic found on US supermarket shelves.
items.title: China-US farm trade reached $14.1 billion in first half of 2026

key_points: A study in India's Western Ghats found that sacred groves hold nearly twice the giant-tree species compared to nearby villages.
These groves act as nurseries, with saplings of large-seeded trees growing under 91% of grove trees versus only 47% in villages.
Experts warn that replacing simple shrines with concrete temples and youth migration threaten these vital ecological refuges.
items.summary: A study published in PLOS One reveals that sacred groves in India's Western Ghats are superior nurseries for future forests compared to surrounding villages. Researchers found these community-protected patches hold nearly twice the giant-tree species and support significantly higher sapling survival rates for large-seeded trees. While groves average just 6,587 square metres, they function as ecological time capsules. However, experts warn that the formalization of shrines into concrete temples and the departure of young people threaten to degrade these unique habitats, which rely on local knowledge and undisturbed ground conditions to sustain biodiversity.
items.title: Sacred Groves in Western Ghats Support Forest Regeneration

key_points: The Supreme Court has requested responses from the Centre, Maharashtra, and Haryana governments regarding a plea to club FIRs against comedian Pranit More.
The controversy stems from a viral comment by an employee during More's show, which led to the comedian's apology and the employee's dismissal.
items.summary: The Supreme Court, comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and other judges, sought responses from the Centre, Maharashtra, and Haryana governments on a plea by comedian Pranit More. More requested the clubbing of FIRs lodged against him in Gurugram and Bombay, stating he had apologized on all forums, including the National Commission for Women. The incident involved a viral comment by an employee, Himanshu Jangra, who allegedly linked a Rs 370 biryani purchase to sexual favors, leading to his dismissal by Starvik Design and widespread social media outrage.
items.title: Supreme Court Seeks Responses on Pranit More's Biryani Remark Case

key_points: BJP Madhya Pradesh Minister Kailash Vijayvargiya faced backlash after telling woman councillor Sandhya Yadav she had gained weight during a public event in Indore.
The remark, captured on video, sparked outrage and criticism from the Congress party, with AICC media coordinator Neelabh Shukla condemning the comment as unacceptable.
items.summary: BJP Madhya Pradesh Cabinet Minister Kailash Vijayvargiya faced controversy after telling woman councillor Sandhya Yadav she had put on weight during an inauguration event in Indore. The comment, captured on video, went viral and drew sharp criticism from the Opposition Congress. AICC media coordinator Neelabh Shukla termed the remark condemnable, highlighting concerns about BJP leaders' recurring comments on women's physical appearance despite the party's stated respect for women.
items.title: BJP Minister Kailash Vijayvargiya Faces Criticism for Body-Shaming Remark

key_points: Senator Mitch McConnell returned to Congress and voted on the agricultural committee, but passage remains unlikely due to Democratic opposition.
Democrats block the bill because it fails to restore SNAP funding cut by $186 billion in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
Without a deal, the nation faces a fourth consecutive year without renewed agricultural policy, potentially forcing states to make difficult budget choices.
items.summary: Senator Mitch McConnell returned to Congress and cast a deciding vote in the Republican-led agricultural committee, yet the Senate farm bill faces a likely dead end. Democrats oppose the current draft because it does not reverse cuts to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, which were slashed by $186 billion last summer. With Republicans holding 53 seats but needing 60 votes to pass legislation, they must sway Democrats before the November midterms. Consequently, the bill is unlikely to pass this year, marking the fourth straight year lawmakers fail to renew the nation's cornerstone agricultural policy. This stalemate forces states to reconsider budgets for education, transportation, and agriculture, while conservation programs face redesign needs. Some advocates argue that avoiding a bad deal might be preferable to passing one, as the absence of a deal delays implementation until 2027.
items.title: Senate Farm Bill Stalls Amid SNAP Funding Dispute and Political Gridlock

key_points: Dr Ashok Seth shared video evidence of a cockroach on a dining table at JW Marriott, sparking public outrage and calls for intervention.
The Maharashtra FDA has conducted over 12,000 inspections in 100 days, issuing thousands of notices and suspending hundreds of licenses to enforce food safety.
items.summary: Fortis Escorts Heart Institute Chief Dr Ashok Seth triggered public outrage by sharing video evidence of a cockroach found on a dining table at the JW Marriott hotel in Mumbai. He urged the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration Commissioner to intervene regarding the hygiene lapse. This incident occurs within the context of an intensive statewide food safety enforcement campaign led by the FDA, which has conducted over 12,000 inspections in 100 days, issued more than 5,000 improvement notices, and suspended approximately 600 licenses to build a compliance culture and protect public health.
items.title: Dr Ashok Seth Exposes Cockroach at JW Marriott Amid FDA Crackdown

key_points: The agreement is set to enter into force on October 20, 2026, featuring tariff removals by New Zealand and reductions by India on 95% of imports.
items.summary: India and New Zealand formally ratified their Free Trade Agreement on September 21, 2026, according to New Zealand's Trade and Investment Minister Todd McClay. The agreement, originally inked in April 2026, will enter into force on October 20, 2026. Under the deal, New Zealand will remove all tariffs on Indian goods, while India will remove or reduce tariffs on 95% of New Zealand imports. McClay highlighted the partnership as a historic step to deepen trade and investment ties.
items.title: India and New Zealand Ratify Historic Free Trade Agreement

key_points: Antonio Guterres is concluding his decade-long tenure as UN Secretary-General at the final General Assembly, marking the end of his two terms.
Observers note that Guterres' legacy is defined by a more divided world, with major power rivalries and vetoes hindering the UN's ability to act on global crises.
items.summary: Antonio Guterres is concluding his decade-long tenure as UN Secretary-General at the final General Assembly, marking the end of his two terms. Observers note that Guterres' legacy is defined by a more divided world, with major power rivalries and vetoes hindering the UN's ability to act on global crises. While facing constraints, Guterres focused on areas like climate change and AI, and brokered the Black Sea Grain Initiative, though critics argue he did not fully wield his moral authority.
items.title: Guterres Concludes UN Tenure Amidst Global Division

key_points: A 55-day basil trial confirmed the system's technical feasibility, while the team notes that long-term agronomic performance and automated nutrient management require further testing.
items.summary: Researchers at Mexico's Northwestern Center for Biological Research (Cibnor) developed Totem, an open-source, solar-powered aeroponic system designed for low-cost, off-grid vertical farming. The system uses a closed recirculation loop and is constructed from commercially available components. A 55-day basil cultivation trial confirmed the system's technical feasibility, supporting two successive harvests. However, the researchers note that long-term agronomic performance and automated nutrient management require further testing.
items.title: Researchers Develop Solar-Powered Off-Grid Vertical Farming System

key_points: The visit, confirmed by Beijing, aims to exchange views on world peace amid the Iran war and strengthen China-US relations through high-level diplomacy.
items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is scheduled to make a three-day state visit to the United States from September 23 to 25, marking his first such trip since 2015. Confirmed by Beijing, the visit aims to exchange views on world peace amid the ongoing Iran war and strengthen bilateral ties. President Xi will meet with US President Donald J. Trump, with the agenda focusing on strategic stability and global peace. The trip includes high-level exchanges and is expected to be received at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland.
items.title: Chinese President Xi to Visit US for World Peace Talks

key_points: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called on France, Canada, the US, and China to cooperate on artificial intelligence regulation.
Carney emphasized the need for joint efforts to ensure AI technology remains safe and effective during a meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron.
items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, speaking with French President Emmanuel Macron in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, urged leading AI nations including France, Canada, the US, and China to collaborate on regulation. Carney stated that these countries must join forces to ensure artificial intelligence is safe and effective. The remarks occurred during Carney's first official visit to the French archipelago, where leaders also agreed to deepen cooperation in strategic sectors like defense and emerging technologies.
items.title: Mark Carney Urges Global AI Cooperation for Safety and Regulation

key_points: The threats were subsequently declared hoaxes after verification, though similar incidents have occurred recently at other public institutions in the city.
items.summary: Several schools in Delhi received bomb threats on Monday morning, prompting the Delhi Police, Delhi Fire Services, and other security agencies to launch search operations. The Delhi Fire Services reported receiving three calls between 9.41 a.m. and 10.50 a.m. regarding threats at Mother International School, Navy Children's School, and Bal Bharati School. After verification, the threats were declared hoaxes, and search operations continued at the affected premises. Officials noted that similar bomb threat emails had targeted schools and public institutions in Delhi in recent weeks.
items.title: Delhi Schools Face Bomb Threats Leading to Search Operations

key_points: Nungambakkam police arrested Selvarani for the death of her husband, Sub Inspector Raji, at their home.
Police allege Selvarani poisoned him with sleeping pills, contradicting her claim of accidental fire.
items.summary: Nungambakkam police arrested Selvarani in connection with the death of her husband, 58-year-old Sub Inspector Raji, at their residence. While Selvarani told police she found him dead in a smoke-filled room caused by an accidental fire, investigators found she had served him food laced with sleeping pills to kill him. Police are currently searching for an accomplice named Deva. The body was sent to the Government Kilpauk Medical College Hospital for a post-mortem.
items.title: Woman Arrested For Murdering Her Husband In Nungambakkam

key_points: The two leaders are expected to hold in-depth exchanges on major issues including trade, tariffs, artificial intelligence, Taiwan, and the war in Iran.
items.summary: China confirmed that President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to the United States from September 23 to 25, at the invitation of President Donald Trump. During the trip, the two leaders are expected to hold in-depth exchanges of views on major issues concerning China-US relations, as well as world peace and development. The reciprocal visits are described as having historic significance, with discussions anticipated on trade, tariffs, artificial intelligence, Taiwan, and the war in Iran.
items.title: President Xi Jinping to Visit US for State Talks

key_points: Since her father Sebastian Scirpo died in 2002, Lisa Scirpo has worked to keep the Middlesex Livestock Auction open as the sole sale barn in Connecticut.
The auction, which began in 1959 when Sebastian made $7 on his first commission, now serves farmers who previously had to travel to Massachusetts or Pennsylvania.
items.summary: Since her father Sebastian Scirpo died in 2002, Lisa Scirpo has worked to preserve the Middlesex Livestock Auction as the only remaining sale barn in Connecticut. The auction, which began in 1959 when Sebastian made $7 on his first commission, now serves farmers who previously had to travel to Massachusetts or Pennsylvania. Lisa, her sister Lana, and their aunt Barbara continue to run the family operation, balancing livestock sales with paperwork and endurance despite Lisa's cancer diagnosis. The family maintains that animals come first, rejecting the view of livestock merely as commodities.
items.title: Lisa Scirpo Preserves Connecticut's Only Livestock Auction

key_points: Australian authorities are intensifying crackdowns on illegal fishing, issuing large fines and destroying boats to combat a global black market estimated to cost legal fisheries up to $23 billion annually.

Prosecutions have surged across Australia, with WA seeing over 273 prosecutions in 2025 and NSW recording 3,767 offences by recreational anglers this year, prompting new legislation and increased surveillance.
items.summary: Australian authorities are intensifying crackdowns on illegal fishing, issuing large fines and destroying boats to combat a global black market estimated to cost legal fisheries up to $23 billion annually. Prosecutions have surged across Australia, with WA seeing over 273 prosecutions in 2025 and NSW recording 3,767 offences by recreational anglers this year, prompting new legislation and increased surveillance. Officials are investing in night vision technology and higher fines, such as up to $44,000 in NSW, to deter poaching of high-value species like mud crabs and abalone that threaten marine ecosystems.
items.title: Australia Cracks Down on Billions in Illegal Fishing

key_points: Seven rebel groups, including the Fano militia and Oromo Liberation Army, announced a new coalition named the Alliance for Survival to remove the Ethiopian government.
items.summary: Seven Ethiopian rebel groups, including the Fano militia and Oromo Liberation Army, announced the formation of the Alliance for Survival to remove the government in Addis Ababa. The coalition accuses Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's administration of presiding over war and genocide, claiming the country faces disintegration. Federal authorities have not yet responded to the announcement. The alliance includes groups from five regions, representing half of Ethiopia's states.
items.title: Seven Ethiopian Rebel Groups Form New Alliance Against Government

key_points: The Joint Chiefs of Staff stated the explosion's cause remains unknown, while Seoul resumed anti-North Korea broadcasts following the incident.
items.summary: Seoul's military reported that three South Korean officers were injured during an operation near the heavily mined border with North Korea. The Joint Chiefs of Staff stated the explosion's cause remains unknown, though it occurred south of the Military Demarcation Line. Two officers were evacuated by helicopter while a third was airlifted. Seoul resumed anti-North Korea loudspeaker broadcasts following the incident, which comes as President Lee Jae-myung seeks dialogue with Pyongyang.
items.title: Three South Korean Soldiers Injured in DMZ Explosion

key_points: The Supreme Court scrapped sweeping interim orders issued by an arbitral tribunal, ruling that the initiation of the proceedings was legally invalid.
The court found the tribunal's appointment lacked consent from the appellants and proceeded despite allegations of bias and close links to the respondent bank.
Consequently, the court quashed the orders freezing bank accounts and seizing properties, directing the return of transferred funds and the appointment of a fresh arbitrator.
items.summary: The Supreme Court of India quashed sweeping interim orders issued by an arbitral tribunal in a dispute between Arth Micro Finance Pvt Ltd and Shivalik Small Finance Bank Ltd. A bench comprising justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran ruled that the initiation of the arbitration was 'non est in law' because there was no evidence the appellants consented to the tribunal's appointment. The court further termed the interim orders, which included freezing bank accounts and seizing properties, as 'arbitrary in nature' given the clear objection to the tribunal's appointment and allegations of bias. Consequently, the court set aside the high court's order, quashed the interim measures, and directed the return of transferred funds within one week. The bench appointed advocate Mayuri Raghuwanshi as a fresh arbitrator to resolve the underlying dispute.
items.title: Supreme Court Quashes Arbitrary Arbitration Orders Due to Appointment Bias

key_points: Volvo Cars has appointed Klaus Zellmer, current CEO of Škoda, as its next president and CEO to lead a turnaround effort amid a 40% share decline.
Zellmer will assume the role by October 2027, succeeding Håkan Samuelsson who is overseeing a cost-cutting plan and strategic restructuring to improve operating margins.
items.summary: Volvo Cars has appointed Klaus Zellmer, the current chief executive of Volkswagen's Škoda brand, as its next president and CEO to lead a turnaround. Zellmer, who brings over three decades of industry experience, will take up the role no later than 1 October 2027. Current CEO Håkan Samuelsson will remain until then to oversee the handover. Volvo's shares have fallen by around 40% this year, prompting the appointment. Samuelsson has implemented a cost and cash plan, cut 3,000 jobs, and adjusted the electrification strategy. Volvo is targeting an operating margin above 8% against 3.
items.title: Volvo Cars Appoints Klaus Zellmer as Next CEO for Turnaround

key_points: IIT Bombay Dean of Administrative Affairs Suryanarayana Doolla has been suspended immediately following a student suicide investigation.
The institute apologized for earlier premature claims regarding the circumstances of the student's death before the investigation concluded.
Students and faculty forums have expressed solidarity with Doolla, rejecting allegations of casteist remarks and affirming he followed protocol.
items.summary: Suryanarayana Doolla, the Dean of Administrative Affairs at IIT Bombay, has been suspended with immediate effect amid an investigation into a student's suicide. IIT Bombay director Shirish B. Kedare stated that further action would follow the probe. The institute later apologized for previous communications that framed the events before the investigation was complete. While the student's family filed a police complaint alleging harassment and casteist slurs, the IIT Bombay Faculty Forum and student groups have defended Doolla, claiming he was merely discharging his duties and following approved procedures when he reported a student using a smartphone during an exam.
items.title: IIT Bombay Dean Suspended Amid Student Suicide Probe

key_points: The arrests followed a police raid on Aleem Khan's home, where his nephews and children were also taken but later released, while the sisters remain detained under public order laws.
items.summary: The three sisters of former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan were arrested in Punjab and sent to Kot Lakhpat Jail in Lahore, his party Tehreek-e-Insaf said on Monday. Punjab police raided Aleem Khan's home, abducting the sisters, his nephews, and their children. While the children were released, the sisters were taken into custody. The deputy commissioner of Lahore passed orders for their 30-day detention under the Maintenance of Public Order law. Punjab police did not respond to requests for comment, and the Information Minister called the party's protest call illegal.
items.title: Sisters of Jailed Pakistani PM Imran Khan Arrested

key_points: The United States has issued a fresh travel warning urging American citizens to leave Iran immediately due to rising tensions and the possibility of further escalation across West Asia.
items.summary: The United States has issued a fresh travel warning urging American citizens to leave Iran immediately due to rising tensions and the possibility of further escalation across West Asia. The U.S. Mission warned of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and attacks on U.S. interests, advising citizens to avoid demonstrations and monitor official communications. The alert cites Iranian-supported Houthi forces and previous attacks on diplomatic facilities as contributing factors to the complex security environment.
items.title: U.S. Issues Urgent Travel Warning for Americans in Iran Amid Regional Tensions

key_points: A former police officer, Beaumont Lamarre-Condon, faces charges for the 2024 murders of his ex-partner and her new partner in Sydney.
Prosecutors allege Lamarre-Condon acted out of jealousy, disguising himself as an Uber driver to enter the victims' home and killing them with a service weapon.
items.summary: A former Sydney police officer, Beaumont Lamarre-Condon, has been charged with two counts of domestic violence-related murder and one count of aggravated break and enter. Prosecutors allege that Lamarre-Condon, driven by a jealous infatuation with his ex-partner Jesse Baird, killed her and her new partner, Luke Davies, in Paddington in 2024. The accused is said to have disguised himself as an Uber driver to gain entry to the home before shooting both victims. Lamarre-Condon pleaded not guilty, and the trial is expected to last three months.
items.title: Former Sydney Police Officer Charged With Double Murder

key_points: Authorities are conducting search operations at three schools in Delhi following bomb threats received on Monday.
items.summary: Three schools in Delhi, specifically Mother International School, Navy Children's School, and Bal Bharti School, received bomb threats on Monday. Police and emergency teams are currently conducting search operations at these locations in Hauz Khas and Chanakyapuri. According to an official from the Delhi Fire Services, a search is underway and nothing suspicious has been found so far. Further details are awaited.
items.title: Three Delhi Schools Receive Bomb Threats Prompting Search Operations

key_points: Alexandr Wang, Meta's highest-paid employee, issued an apology after making a humorous remark regarding flight booking via the company's AI tool.
Meta launched Muse, an autonomous AI agent designed to handle tasks like travel arrangements, which was tested by a WebFlow executive.
items.summary: Alexandr Wang, identified as Meta's highest-paid employee, posted an apology on X after making a joke about flight booking while responding to a WebFlow CTO's post. The executive had successfully used Meta's autonomous AI agent, Muse, to arrange travel. Wang initially celebrated the milestone before adding a humorous suggestion to book a return flight, which he later clarified was a 'dumb joke.' Muse, launched earlier in the month, aims to provide personal superintelligence by executing tasks like booking travel and sending emails.
items.title: Meta's top employee apologizes for joke about AI travel booking

key_points: Commodity vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz declined to a dozen this weekend, compared to 35 a week earlier.
While overall traffic drops, Saudi crude exports via Hormuz remain strong at 2.9 million barrels daily despite pipeline disruptions.
items.summary: Reuters reports that commodity vessels traversing the Strait of Hormuz declined further, with just a dozen making the passage this weekend compared to 35 a week earlier. While overall traffic drops, JP Morgan notes tanker traffic is improving, especially in Saudi Arabia. The investment bank stated that Middle East oil flows remain surprisingly strong despite the disruption to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, with exports reaching 2.9 million barrels daily over the past six days via Hormuz.
items.title: Shipping Traffic Falls as Saudi Oil Flows Rise via Hormuz

key_points: Authorities stated the man was hospitalized in life-threatening condition while the officer was also taken to a hospital, with no immediate threat to public safety.
items.summary: On Sunday, September 20, 2026, a police officer and a man were wounded during a gunfire exchange near the Sons of Jacob Synagogue in Belleville, Ontario, as the Jewish community observed Yom Kippur. Authorities confirmed the man was hospitalized in life-threatening condition and the officer was taken to a hospital. The Special Investigations Unit and Belleville police are investigating the incident, which occurred about 110 miles east of Toronto. Ontario Premier Doug Ford expressed disgust over the shooting and called for the arrest of those responsible, while York Regional Police noted increased patrols at places of worship.
items.title: Shooting Near Ontario Synagogue Leaves Officer and Man Wounded on Yom Kippur

key_points: The company noted the program is at an early validation stage with no current orders, citing highly uncertain prospects for large-scale commercialization.
items.summary: Chinese PV manufacturer JA launched its internally developed p-type heterojunction photovoltaic modules into orbit aboard a Kuaizhou-11 rocket to begin validating the technology for commercial space power systems. The modules, hosted as payloads on remote-sensing satellites, will undergo testing for long-term reliability under low Earth orbit conditions. JA stated the program remains at an early validation stage with no current orders and highly uncertain prospects for large-scale commercialization.
items.title: JA Launches Heterojunction PV Modules for Space Validation

key_points: Police reported that CCTV footage captured the accused shoving a constable away before jumping from the railing, and authorities are investigating potential security lapses.
items.summary: Shashidhar, a 49-year-old physical education teacher arrested for alleged sexual assault of children under the POCSO Act, died after jumping from the third floor of the Bengaluru South SP office complex in Ramanagara while in judicial custody. Police stated that CCTV footage showed the accused shoving a constable away before jumping from a railing. He sustained serious injuries and was pronounced dead at the district hospital. Authorities are currently investigating the circumstances of the incident and potential security lapses during his escort.
items.title: POCSO-accused teacher jumps to death from Bengaluru SP office while in custody

key_points: Young Moroccans who led recent Gen Z protests are now participating in parliamentary elections, with former demonstrators running for seats.
Youth unemployment stands at 37% among those aged 15 to 24, while this demographic represents only 4% of registered voters despite making up 12% of the population.
items.summary: Morocco is preparing for its first parliamentary elections since deadly Gen Z demonstrations, with young people who previously protested now turning to the ballot box. Former participants, including candidates like Younes Belaidi and Aymane Saissi, are running for seats in the House of Representatives. Official data indicates youth unemployment among those aged 15 to 24 is 37%, significantly higher than the overall rate of 13%. Although youth aged 18 to 24 make up 12% of the population, they account for only 4% of the 15.8 million registered voters.
items.title: Moroccan Youth Turn to Ballot Box After Protests

key_points: US President Donald Trump faces a critical decision regarding potential military action against Iran as the regional conflict widens into its seventh month.
The Iran-backed Houthis have escalated attacks on Saudi Arabia, damaging critical oil infrastructure and threatening the viability of the new Mecca pact with Turkey and Pakistan.
Trump has expressed a desire to end the conflict before the US mid-term elections but has so far rebuffed requests for direct US strikes against the Houthis.
items.summary: As the conflict in the Middle East enters its seventh month, Saudi Arabia's newly formed defence agreement with Turkey and Pakistan faces its first serious test. The Iran-backed Houthis recently attacked sensitive sites in Riyadh and damaged a major oil pipeline, disrupting 70% of Saudi oil exports. While US President Donald Trump has indicated he is considering a major decision regarding Iran, he has rebuffed Saudi requests for direct strikes against the Houthis. Trump aims to conclude the war before the November mid-term elections, though uncertainty remains regarding the conflict's trajectory and the reliability of US security guarantees for Gulf states.
items.title: Saudi Arabia's New Defence Pact Faces Test Amid Escalating Regional Conflict

key_points: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty climbed in early trade driven by falling oil prices and foreign fund inflows.
Major Sensex stocks like UltraTech Cement and InterGlobe Aviation led gains while Infosys and Adani Ports lagged.
items.summary: Indian stock market benchmarks Sensex and Nifty rose in early trade on Monday amid cooling crude oil prices and fresh foreign fund inflows. The Sensex jumped 448.32 points to 74,743.28, while the Nifty gained 50.3 points to 23,396.70. Brent crude fell 2.25% to $101.5 per barrel. Foreign Institutional Investors bought equities worth ₹599.54 crore on Friday. Major Sensex winners included UltraTech Cement and InterGlobe Aviation, while Infosys and Adani Ports were laggards. Regional Asian markets also posted gains.
items.title: Indian Stock Markets Rise on Oil Drop and Foreign Buying

key_points: The charter demands an independent investigation, professor accountability, and an interim report by September 30, while police have registered an FIR under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
items.summary: IIT Bombay Director Shireesh Kedare signed an 18-point charter presented by protesting students following the suicide of a second-year student named Sahil Wakode. The students, who held a sit-in for three days, demanded an independent investigation and action. Key demands include the suspension of Professor Suryanarayana Doolla and a public apology. Meanwhile, the Mumbai Crime Branch took over the investigation, registering an FIR under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The charter also seeks an interim report by September 30.
items.title: IIT Bombay Director Signs Student Charter After Suicide Protest

key_points: The Election Commission stated that over 5,000 names were duplicate entries while 29,940 voters had died, accounting for 11.7% of the electorate.
items.summary: PTI reported that over 1. 5 lakh persons were removed from Nagaland's draft voter list during a special intensive revision. The state's voter count dropped from 13. 5 lakh to 11. 9 lakh. Reasons included 1. 2 lakh voters marked as shifted or absent, 29,940 deaths, and over 5,000 duplicate entries, totaling 11. 7% of the electorate. The Election Commission noted that objections can be filed until October 20, with appeals heard by November 18 before the final roll publication on November 22.
items.title: Nagaland Removes Over 1.5 Lakh Voters in Draft List Revision

key_points: Sunday's regional elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin resulted in severe losses for the ruling CDU, with the far-right AfD becoming the strongest party in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who described the outcome as a disaster, faces mounting pressure to deliver on reforms and keep the AfD at bay amid low approval ratings.

The AfD gained significantly in both states, consolidating its leading position, while coalition-building becomes tougher as voters split across more parties and traditional two-party governments face challenges.
items.summary: Sunday's regional elections in Germany resulted in severe losses for the ruling CDU, with Chancellor Friedrich Merz describing the outcome as a disaster. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the far-right AfD became the strongest party, more than doubling its result compared with 2021, while the hard-left Die Linke led the polls in Berlin. Merz, facing the lowest approval ratings since records began, is under pressure to deliver on promised reforms as calls mount for him to resign. The AfD, already the strongest party in nationwide polls with 29 percent, has drawn support for pledges of tough action on immigration and returning to cheap Russian energy. Coalition-building is getting tougher as stable majorities become harder to build, requiring more willingness to compromise in a country that has traditionally run on two-party governments. The Greens and Social Democratic Party are exploring alternative coalition arrangements to form a majority in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
items.title: German Regional Elections Signal Setback for Chancellor Merz and CDU

key_points: Foreign students currently make up 11.6% of Italian school enrollment, according to data cited by Reuters.
items.summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced plans to ban burqas and niqabs in schools and limit the number of foreign students in each class. The measures would also require parents of foreign students facing integration difficulties to attend Italian language classes. Meloni stated these plans at a gathering of the Brothers of Italy party in Rome. Currently, foreign students account for 11.6% of those enrolled in Italian schools.
items.title: Italy Plans Burqa Ban and Foreign Student Limits in Schools

key_points: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that US and Chinese officials discussed creating a notification mechanism for AI incidents affecting national security.
The talks occurred in New York ahead of a summit between President Trump and Xi Jinping in Washington.
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reported that US and Chinese officials discussed establishing a notification mechanism for AI incidents impacting national security. Bessent described the talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York as successful. These discussions took place ahead of a summit between President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping scheduled for later in the week in Washington.
items.title: US and China Discuss AI Safety Mechanism Ahead of Trump-Xi Summit

key_points: Crude oil prices dropped to a weekly low as traders anticipated a diplomatic resolution to the Middle East conflict, despite a lack of evidence for negotiations.
Saudi Arabia reported a significant increase in daily oil exports via the Strait of Hormuz, contrasting with previous lower figures from August.
items.summary: Crude oil prices declined to a weekly low driven by renewed hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Middle East war, even though no evidence supports negotiations. While the U.S. and Iran exchanged threats and Yemeni Houthis escalated attacks on Saudi Arabia, traders pinned hopes on a UN meeting. Analyst Tim Waterer noted a risk premium removal from prices. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia redirected flows, achieving 2.9 million barrels daily via the Strait of Hormuz, up from 700,000 barrels in August, according to JP Morgan.
items.title: Oil Prices Fall on Diplomatic Hopes Amid Middle East Tensions

key_points: Sensex gained 550 points to 74,850 while Nifty rose 78 points to 23,422 on Monday, though broader markets slipped.
Analysts note that while geopolitical risks increase, falling oil prices may support a short-lived consolidation before a potential rise to 23,560.
items.summary: Sensex gained 550 points to 74,850, and Nifty rose 78 points to trade near 23,422 on Monday, as oil prices cooled despite Middle East tensions. Broader markets slipped, with Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 falling up to 0.4%. Analysts V K Vijayakumar and Anand James of Geojit Investments noted that while geopolitical risks are increasing, Brent crude has declined below $102 per barrel. They expect Nifty to consolidate near the 23,400 objective before potentially rising to 23,560 if dips are contained.
items.title: Sensex and Nifty rise as oil prices cool despite Middle East tensions

key_points: NVIDIA highlighted five companies at New York Climate Week that are using AI to overcome barriers in clean energy adoption.
ThinkLabs and Redwood Materials are using AI to speed up grid interconnections and power AI factories with recycled batteries.
TerraPower and Atomic Canyon are applying AI to nuclear operations, while Commonwealth Fusion Systems is using it to compress fusion research timelines.
items.summary: At New York Climate Week, NVIDIA highlighted five companies leveraging AI to accelerate clean energy adoption by addressing infrastructure and cost barriers. ThinkLabs uses digital twins to reduce grid interconnection evaluation time from weeks to minutes, while Redwood Materials employs AI to integrate repurposed EV batteries for off-grid AI factory power. In the nuclear sector, Atomic Canyon streamlines operations with AI knowledge management, and TerraPower uses digital twins to speed up plant delivery. Meanwhile, Commonwealth Fusion Systems utilizes NVIDIA Omniverse to compress fusion research timelines, aiming for grid-ready fusion energy in the 2030s.
items.title: Five Companies Use NVIDIA AI to Accelerate Clean Energy Projects

key_points: 24/7 Wall St. analysts lowered AMD's 12-month price target to $510.66, citing a trailing P/E of 211 that implies 9% downside despite recent revenue growth.
The firm notes that while AMD's Data Center revenue doubled year-over-year, its valuation remains dangerously stretched compared to NVIDIA's 45x earnings multiple.
items.summary: 24/7 Wall St. analysts have lowered their 12-month price target for AMD to $510.66, implying roughly 9% downside from the current trading price of $559.82. The firm cites a trailing P/E of 211 as a key concern, noting that NVIDIA trades at just 45x earnings with 75% gross margins. Although AMD's Data Center revenue doubled 107% year-over-year to $6.72 billion, the analysts argue the stock is fully priced for perfect execution on Helios and Instinct products. The report recommends holding the stock with high confidence, though it warns that real upside could only come from faster-than-expected AI accelerator deployments.
items.title: 24/7 Wall St. Lowers AMD Price Target Amid High Valuation Concerns

key_points: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and xAI face a lawsuit in California alleging they conspired to slow AI development, potentially harming competition and customers.
items.summary: A lawsuit filed in the US alleges that OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and xAI conspired to deliberately slow AI development. Paid users of ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Gemini brought the case, claiming reduced competition and customer harm. Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Meta's Mark Zuckerberg oppose slowing development, while former President Trump called the request a 'deception'.
items.title: Four major AI companies sued in US for allegedly slowing development

key_points: The article argues that Nvidia remains a strong investment despite recent market cooling, citing accelerating growth forecasts and potential benefits from easing trade restrictions with China.
Analysts highlight Nvidia's projected revenue growth and the possibility of new market access as key drivers for a potential stock rebound in the autumn.
items.summary: This article presents three reasons to consider buying Nvidia stock in the fall. It notes that while interest in the company has cooled, its projected revenue growth is accelerating significantly through fiscal 2027. The piece also suggests that Nvidia may benefit from potential easing of trade restrictions with China, which currently blocks sales to that market. The author argues that these factors could make the stock a good investment opportunity despite recent performance lags.
items.title: Three Reasons to Buy Nvidia Shares in the Fall

key_points: A three-month pilot led by Google and partners Quintrace, esVolta, and LevelTen Energy successfully demonstrated the use of Granular Certificates to track renewable energy in hourly intervals for battery storage systems.
The project created the first environmental revenue stream for battery assets by shifting solar energy to hours of high fossil generation, verified against the EnergyTag standard.
The pilot involved a total of 9.2GWh of energy charged and discharged, proving a commercial pathway for carbon-based revenue while maintaining operator control over assets.
items.summary: A three-month pilot sponsored by Google and partners including Quintrace, esVolta, and LevelTen Energy has demonstrated a new method for hourly carbon accounting in US battery storage systems. Announced on 17 September, the project utilized Granular Certificates to allocate solar energy to grid-connected batteries, shifting it to hours when Google's energy consumption exceeded renewable supply. This approach created the first environmental revenue stream for battery energy storage systems (BESS) assets. Over the pilot period, the batteries charged and discharged a total of 9.2GWh during defined windows, with each hour verified against the EnergyTag standard. The structure maintained operator control over assets while providing a commercial pathway for carbon-based revenue.
items.title: Google-Backed Pilot Demonstrates Hourly Carbon Accounting for US Battery Storage

key_points: The Eurosystem launched Pontes to allow banks to settle tokenised asset trades using central bank money, addressing a key barrier for blockchain adoption.
Thirteen institutions are ready to use the system immediately, while the ECB plans to invest its own funds in tokenised securities through it.
items.summary: The Eurosystem has launched Pontes, a system enabling banks to settle trades in tokenised assets using central bank money. This initiative aims to remove the risk-free settlement asset barrier hindering blockchain technology. Thirteen institutions, including Deutsche Bank and Clearstream, are ready to use the system immediately. Additionally, the ECB intends to invest its own funds in tokenised securities through Pontes, focusing initially on euro-denominated debt. The system is designed for wholesale transactions rather than consumer payments, distinguishing it from the digital euro project.
items.title: ECB launches Pontes system for tokenised asset settlement

key_points: Microsoft launched a new data center in Hyderabad as part of its $20.5 billion AI investment plan in India.
items.summary: Microsoft launched a new data center in Hyderabad as part of its $20.5 billion AI investment plan in India. The facility serves as the company's fourth cloud region in the country and is designed to support AI workloads for Asian and global southern markets. Microsoft President Puneet Chandok stated that the center will help major Indian companies like Adani Group and HDFC Bank leverage cloud services.
items.title: Microsoft Opens Hyderabad Data Center as Part of $20.5 Billion AI Plan

key_points: Reports suggest Apple may skip the iPhone 19 name for its next flagship, potentially calling it the iPhone 20 to mark the device's 20th anniversary.
items.summary: Reports indicate Apple is considering skipping the iPhone 19 name for its next flagship, potentially launching the iPhone 20 to mark the device's 20th anniversary. Leakers suggest the iPhone 20 Pro models could feature larger quad-curved displays, smaller Dynamic Islands, and 2nm chips. However, the launch is nearly a year away, with more details expected before the anticipated 2027 arrival.
items.title: Apple Rumoured to Skip iPhone 19 Name for 20th Anniversary Model

key_points: Microsoft warned that the September 2026 security updates may cause the built-in File History backup feature in Windows to stop working on some systems.
items.summary: Microsoft warned that the September 2026 security updates may cause the built-in File History backup feature in Windows to stop working on some systems. Affected users might see application crash events in Event Viewer, incorrect drive reconnection messages, or backup timestamps that fail to update. The issue impacts Windows 10 and Windows 11 releases. Microsoft confirmed that previous emergency updates did not resolve all audio problems introduced by these updates and is still working on a fix for the remaining issues.
items.title: Microsoft Warns September 2026 Updates May Break File History Backups

key_points: Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined Google €403 million for processing location data without adequate user consent, potentially influencing ads and inferring interests.
The inquiry began in 2020 after complaints from European consumer rights groups, marking the fourth largest fine issued by the Irish regulator.
items.summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined Google €403 million ($463 million) on September 21, 2026, regarding its processing of location data. The regulator stated that Google's failures could leave individuals unaware their location was used to influence ads or infer interests. The inquiry started in 2020 following complaints from European consumer rights organizations. DPC Deputy Commissioner Graham Doyle noted that retaining data longer than necessary aggravated the loss of control. Google did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
items.title: Irish Regulator Fines Google €403 Million Over Location Data

key_points: Indian consumers are traveling to Dubai to purchase the iPhone 18 Pro and Max because prices there are significantly lower than in India.
The price gap, ranging from ₹33,000 to ₹38,000 for single devices, often outweighs flight and visa costs, especially for multiple purchases.
Experts note that tax structures and cross-border arbitrage are driving this trend, though customs rules and travel expenses remain critical factors.
items.summary: Indian consumers are increasingly flying to Dubai to purchase the iPhone 18 Pro and Max due to significant price disparities. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at approximately ₹1.32 lakh in the UAE compared to ₹1.64 lakh in India, a difference of about ₹33,000. Buyers like Aman Solanki and Mohammed Sayed report that these savings cover travel and visa costs, particularly when purchasing multiple devices. Experts attribute the gap to differing tax structures, with India's import duties adding to the cost. While Malaysia and Thailand also offer lower prices, Dubai remains a primary destination for those already planning travel. However, buyers must consider customs allowances and total travel expenses when calculating the true savings.
items.title: Indian Buyers Fly to Dubai for Cheaper iPhones

key_points: Apple reportedly announced layoffs affecting the audio-content team within its Fitness+ division, potentially slowing new feature releases.
The cuts align with a broader strategy to streamline operations and redirect resources toward core artificial intelligence projects.
items.summary: Reports indicate that Apple has announced a second round of layoffs, specifically targeting the audio-content team within its Fitness+ division. This move is expected to slow the release of new features like Time to Walk and Time to Run. According to Bloomberg, the restructuring follows a previous reduction of over 200 roles in August, as Apple shifts resources toward its core artificial intelligence roadmap and Intelligent Personal Hub strategy. While the audio features may see a slower cadence, the main video catalogue and apps will continue normally.
items.title: Apple Announces Layoffs in Fitness+ Audio Team Amid AI Shift

key_points: A new report by environmental groups states Nvidia's supply chain emissions rose by 725% since 2020, driven by upstream manufacturing and materials.
The report estimates operating Nvidia chips sold since 2022 could generate between four and 21 million tonnes of carbon dioxide in 2025, comparable to Russian state coal production.
items.summary: A report by environmental and civil society groups claims Nvidia's supply chain emissions have surged by 725% since 2020, driven by upstream manufacturing. The authors estimate that operating Nvidia chips sold since 2022 could generate between four and 21 million tonnes of carbon dioxide in 2025, comparable to Russian state coal production.
